$comment: Operating choices layered over the world without editing it. The flow record is a PATCH of a declared entity — it merges before expansion (SPEC §8 step 2), so the generator compiles the new direction. The queue record is an OVERRIDE of a derived entity — it applies after expansion (step 4).

entities.$comment: Aisle 1 runs eastbound this scenario. 'patch' means: this record must hit an entity an earlier layer declared — a mistyped UUID is a load error, not a silent half-formed entity. Only the named component is replaced; region and tiling are untouched. A contraflow experiment is this file with '-x'.

Hold EasyLoop 1's queue to the last four cells of its horseshoe this run: the path IS the admission, so a scenario that admits fewer states a shorter path, and the two the run gives up are the two the entry leg starts on. The cells themselves are still floor — the queue simply does not name them. Replacement is wholesale, so path and discipline are restated — the price of predictable merges. Post-expansion, path entries are full chained derivation addresses; the template's local_ref form is meaningless out here.
